ei.title: Thinking with AI, Not Instead of It
ei.subject: AIHumanMind

fullPassage: Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. In his 2024 book Co-Intelligence, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick contends that the true opportunity lies not in whether we use AI, but in how we choose to use it. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for human judgment, Mollick describes it as a kind of thinking partner—one capable of helping us explore ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page. The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment remains firmly in control.

questions.passage: Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. In his 2024 book Co-Intelligence, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick ①<u>contends</u> that the true opportunity lies not in whether we use AI, but in how we choose to use it. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for human judgment, Mollick ②<u>describe</u> it as a kind of thinking partner—one capable of helping us explore ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page. The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise ③<u>spend</u> on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment ④<u>remains</u> firmly in control.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① contends=주장한다(단수주어 정상), ② describe→describes 오류(주어 Mollick은 3인칭 단수), ③ spend=쓰다(복수주어 정상), ④ remains=유지한다(단수주어 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① contends: 'Ethan Mollick contends that ~' — 주어 Mollick(3인칭 단수)에 맞춘 현재형, 정상
✅ ② describe: 'Mollick describes it as a kind of thinking partner'가 맞음. 주어 Mollick이 3인칭 단수이므로 describes가 와야 함. describe는 수 일치 오류 ← 정답
❌ ③ spend: 'we might otherwise spend' — 조동사 might 뒤 동사원형, 정상
❌ ④ remains: 'human judgment remains firmly in control' — 단수 주어에 맞춘 현재형, 정상
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(Mollick)에는 동사에 -s. 'Mollick describes' — describe(X), describes(O)

questions.passage: Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without ③<u>pause</u> to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth ④<u>asking</u> in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment remains firmly in control.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① to use=사용하는 것(choose+to부정사 정상), ② helping=돕는 것(of+동명사 정상), ③ pause→pausing 오류(전치사 without 뒤 동명사), ④ asking=묻는 것(worth+동명사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① to use: 'how we choose to use it' — choose+to부정사, 정상
❌ ② helping: 'one capable of helping us' — 전치사 of 뒤 동명사, 정상
✅ ③ pause: 'without pausing to question it'가 맞음. 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 하므로 pause는 오류 ← 정답
❌ ④ asking: 'which questions are worth asking' — worth 뒤 동명사, 정상
det.tip: 전치사(without) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing). 'without pausing' — pause(X), pausing(O)

questions.passage: Not every researcher believes that ①<u>increased</u> reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. In his 2024 book Co-Intelligence, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick contends that the true opportunity lies not in whether we use AI, but in how we choose to use it. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for human judgment, Mollick describes it as a kind of thinking partner—one capable of helping us explore ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page. The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. ②<u>Using</u> actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, ③<u>allowing</u> us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither ④<u>to compete</u> with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment remains firmly in control.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① increased=증가된(과거분사 형용사 정상), ② Using→Used 오류(AI가 사용되는 수동 분사구문), ③ allowing=~하면서(현재분사 정상), ④ to compete=경쟁하는 것(to부정사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① increased: 'increased reliance on AI' — 명사를 앞에서 꾸미는 과거분사, 정상
✅ ② Using: 'Used actively, ~ AI can free up the time'이 맞음. AI가 '능동적으로 사용될 때'라는 수동의 분사구문이므로 과거분사 Used가 와야 함. Using(능동)은 오류 ← 정답
❌ ③ allowing: 'allowing us to focus on ~' — 부대상황을 나타내는 현재분사, 정상
❌ ④ to compete: 'neither to compete with AI' — to부정사, 정상
det.tip: AI가 '사용되는' 수동 관계 → 과거분사 Used. 'Used actively' — Using(X), Used(O)

Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on ③<u>which</u> machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① whether=~인지(명사절 정상), ② move=넘어가다(help+목적어+원형 정상), ③ which→what 오류(선행사 없는 관계대명사는 what), ④ remains=유지한다(단수주어 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① whether: 'not in whether we use AI' — 전치사 in의 목적어인 명사절을 이끄는 whether, 정상
❌ ② move: 'helping us explore ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page' — help+목적어+원형이 병렬로 이어진 동사원형, 정상
✅ ③ which: 'focus on what machines still cannot do well'이 맞음. 선행사가 없고 '~하는 것'을 뜻하므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 와야 함. which는 선행사가 필요하므로 오류 ← 정답
❌ ④ remains: 'human judgment remains firmly in control' — 단수 주어에 맞춘 현재형, 정상
det.tip: 선행사 없이 '~하는 것' → 관계대명사 what. 'focus on what machines cannot do' — which(X), what(O)

questions.passage: Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. In his 2024 book Co-Intelligence, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick contends that the true opportunity lies not in whether we use AI, but in how we choose to use it. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for human judgment, Mollick describes it as a kind of thinking partner—one capable of helping us ①<u>ignore</u> ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page. The real ②<u>danger</u>, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on ③<u>routine</u> tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment remains firmly in ④<u>control</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① ignore→explore 오류(AI는 아이디어를 탐색하도록 돕는다), ② danger=위험, ③ routine=일상적인, ④ control=통제
det.analysis:
✅ ① ignore: 'helping us ignore ideas rapidly'는 부적절. AI는 아이디어를 '탐색(explore)'하도록 돕는다는 이점을 설명하는 맥락이므로 explore가 맞음. ignore(무시하다)는 정반대 ← 정답
❌ ② danger: 'The real danger ~ is passive engagement' — 진짜 '위험'이라는 맥락, 적절
❌ ③ routine: 'spend on routine tasks' — '일상적' 업무라는 맥락, 적절
❌ ④ control: 'human judgment remains firmly in control' — '통제'를 유지한다는 맥락, 적절
det.tip: helping us explore ideas = 아이디어를 탐색하도록 도움. ignore(무시하다)로 바꾸면 AI의 이점과 모순

The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can ③<u>waste</u> the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① reliance=의존, ② judgment=판단, ③ waste→free up 오류(AI는 시간과 에너지를 '확보해' 준다), ④ cultivate=기르다
det.analysis:
❌ ① reliance: 'increased reliance on AI' — AI에 대한 '의존'이라는 맥락, 적절
❌ ② judgment: 'a substitute for human judgment' — 인간의 '판단'이라는 맥락, 적절
✅ ③ waste: 'AI can waste the time and mental energy'는 부적절. AI를 능동적으로 쓰면 시간과 에너지를 '확보해(free up)' 우리가 더 중요한 일에 집중하게 한다는 맥락이므로 free up이 맞음. waste(낭비하다)는 정반대 ← 정답
❌ ④ cultivate: 'cultivate a working relationship' — 협업 관계를 '기른다'는 맥락, 적절
det.tip: free up the time = 시간을 확보하다. waste(낭비하다)로 바꾸면 뒤의 '집중하게 한다'는 이점과 모순

questions.stem: AI 의존이 커지면 인간의 사고가 반드시 약해진다는 견해에 모든 연구자가 동의하는 것은 아니다.

det.korean: AI 의존 증가와 사고 약화에 대한 연구자들의 견해
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought' — 모든 연구자가 그렇게 믿는 것은 아니라는 내용과 일치

det.tip: Not every researcher believes ~ = 모든 연구자가 ~라고 믿는 것은 아니다(부분부정)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 진짜 위험 = 기계의 첫 답을 의문 없이 받아들이는 '수동적 관여'
det.analysis:
❌ ① constant improvement — 지속적 개선. 뒤에 이어지는 '의문 없이 첫 답을 수용'과 반대되는 긍정 개념

✅ ④ passive engagement — 수동적 관여. 뒤의 '기계의 첫 답을 의문 없이 받아들이는 것'이라는 부연과 정확히 부합 ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: AI가 사고의 동반자로서 돕는 일 — 시작의 막막함을 넘어서게 함
det.analysis:
✅ ① move past a blank page — 빈 페이지를 넘어서다. '아이디어를 빠르게 탐색하고, 주장을 검증하거나, 간단히 ___'로 이어지는 사고 동반자의 역할에 부합. 시작의 막막함을 극복하도록 돕는다는 의미 ← 정답

❌ ③ guarantee correct answers — 정답을 보장하다. 첫 답을 의심하라는 글과 모순
❌ ④ avoid all mistakes — 모든 실수를 피하다. 본문에 근거 없는 과장
det.tip: explore ideas, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page = 아이디어 탐색·주장 검증·시작의 막막함 극복

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문과 일치하지 않는 선지 찾기

questions.passage: Not every researcher believes that increased reliance on AI must inevitably weaken human thought. In his 2024 book Co-Intelligence, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick contends that the true opportunity lies not in whether we use AI, but in how we choose to use it. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for human judgment, Mollick describes it as a kind of thinking partner—one capable of helping us explore ideas rapidly, test arguments, or simply move past a blank page. The real danger, he suggests, is not the technology itself but passive engagement with it: accepting a machine's first response without pausing to question it. Used actively, he argues, AI can free up the time and mental energy that we might otherwise spend on routine tasks, allowing us to focus on what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking in the first place. In this view, the goal is neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely, but to cultivate a working relationship in which human judgment remains firmly in control.

❌ ③ 불일치: 'what machines still cannot do well—namely, determining which questions are worth asking' — 그 판단은 기계가 못 하는 일
❌ ④ 불일치: 'neither to compete with AI nor to depend on it entirely' — 경쟁도 전적 의존도 목표가 아님
det.tip: 진짜 기회 = 사용 여부(whether)가 아니라 사용 방식(how). 나머지는 본문과 반대
